content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) SPRINT outcomes demonstrated that targeting a more intensive systolic blood pressure (SBP) goal resulted in a 25% reduction in the risk of the primary composite endpoint, which includes myocardial infarction (MI), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), stroke, heart failure, and cardiovascular death. Additionally, there was a 27% decrease in all-cause mortality associated with this intensive SBP management. However, this approach was also associated with an increased risk of electrolyte abnormalities and acute kidney injury (AKI).
